### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and 
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close #36636

Problem Summary:

Lift the limitation of only supporting a single column in RANGE COLUMNS partitioning

### What is changed and how it works?

For partition pruning I reused the ranger.DetachCondAndBuildRangeForIndex to get ranges from the conditions and then binary search for finding which partitions would match.

For mapping data to partitions, I only tested and fixed the existing implementation in table/tables/partition.go

### Release note

<!-- compatibility change, improvement, bugfix, and new feature need a release note -->

Please refer to [Release Notes Language Style Guide](https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/release-notes-style-guide.html) to write a quality release note.

```

issue_context.title: Support multi-column RANGE COLUMNS partitioning
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement

Currently is only one column supported for RANGE COLUMNS partitioning, we should be compatible with MySQL and support multiple columns.

review_comments:
Add it to bench daily so we can see the result like this http://www.zenlife.tk:18081/? 

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/8b5b724d8a932239303a1d0ba547323eb0e5161b/executor/union_scan_test.go#L565
Could you explain why get why `if isNull` is removed here? '// If the column value used to determine the partition is NULL, the row is inserted into the lowest partition.' is commented in line 1018.

If the value from the row is NULL (or really if the partitioning expression evaluates to NULL) it is already compared during the search and idx will already become 0.
A partition definition value (`partitionExprs`) can never be NULL, so the generated expression (comparison between partition definition value and column (or partition expression)) can only be NULL if the column is NULL (or the partition expression evaluates to NULL.

I wonder if we should also propagate if there is an error during the Search? Like creating a `hadError bool` variable and setting it to true if `err != nil` and use that at line 1025/1024 instead, since the current `err` is only from the last call during the binary `sort.Search`. (Actually the same affects the isNull value anyway...)
[sort.Search()](https://pkg.go.dev/sort#Search) return values in the range of [0,n), so it cannot happen.

I still do not understand why `multi-column use new evaluated+normalized output`?  look like it is not compatibility with mysql:

```sql
create table t(a time, b time) partition by range columns (a, b) (partition p1 values less than ('2020', '2020'), partition p2 values less than ('20:20:10', '20:20:10'));
```

then, `show create table` result in MySQL 8.0 is:
```sql
mysql>show create table t\G
***************************[ 1. row ]***************************
Table        | t
Create Table | CREATE TABLE `t` (
  `a` time DEFAULT NULL,
  `b` time DEFAULT NULL
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci
/*!50500 PARTITION BY RANGE  COLUMNS(a,b)
(PARTITION p1 VALUES LESS THAN ('2020','2020') ENGINE = InnoDB,
 PARTITION p2 VALUES LESS THAN ('20:20:10','20:20:10') ENGINE = InnoDB) */
``` 

As you can see, MySQL keep use the original value in `PARTITION p1 VALUES LESS THAN ('2020','2020')`

The result in TiDB with this PR is:
```sql
mysql>show create table t\G
***************************[ 1. row ]***************************
Table        | t
Create Table | CREATE TABLE `t` (
  `a` time DEFAULT NULL,
  `b` time DEFAULT NULL
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_bin
PARTITION BY RANGE COLUMNS(`a`,`b`)
(PARTITION `p1` VALUES LESS THAN ('00:20:20','00:20:20'),
 PARTITION `p2` VALUES LESS THAN ('20:20:10','20:20:10'))
```

But TiDB will use a converted value in `PARTITION `p1` VALUES LESS THAN ('00:20:20','00:20:20')`

It is to make it more user friendly. The output is still compatible with MySQL, meaning the output is still valid syntax, just more readable. I did not change it for the existing single column RANGE COLUMNS, but only for this new implementation, to avoid having to do it in a new feature request. Also it replaces the `expression.Format()` call on the original expression, to a `value.String()` from the validation step, where the expression is already evaluated and checked.

In your example it is much more clear that '00:20:00' is a time value, rather than '2020' which needs the context of the column type as time and some mental parsing and mysql knowledge to understand that it means the same.

I see this more of a nice to have, which makes the feature better (better readability). It is not necessary from a technical point.

@crazycs520 do you want me to remove this to make the output the same as MySQL or do you see any value of having the partition definition values evaluated and normalized?

In my opinion, line #1193 ~ #1208 make the logic here more complicated, and the complicated is not necessary.
For compatibility or make it more user-friendly, how about asking for PM's opinion first?
After discussing with @bb7133 and PM @moyun, they prefer the currently user-friendly implementation, I agree too.

haha, just a name :) I think I copy pasted the line, since I wanted one more partition and just changed the name...
I can change it if you want?
Btw, it was added here:
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/29945/files#diff-650c6df5588c92cf04db6f27af4327d648ddbfb2ffcf028a013237530014c6c0R1139
And the row change was to fix the issue that the same column cannot have MAXVALUE if the previous column has not changed from the previous partition, i.e. the partition's VALUE LESS THAN (expr) must increase for each partition.

Since the other implementations are using the `expr.Format()` (line 1208) to format a string, and that will wrap in in single quotes ([see here](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/f89609d018c5ec2a884212b6bbc653f78ec98c3a/types/parser_driver/value_expr.go#L170)).
